<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915961_theRebbe_461" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915961_theRebbe_461__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Motzaei Shabbos Kodesh Parshas Mikeitz,</t>
    <t s="2">the night of this Chanukah, 5746*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the eight days of Chanukah parallel the eight days of the inauguration, with the eighth day of Chanukah being called "Zos Chanukah" and corresponding to Malchus.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"On the eighth day, the prince of the children of Menasheh..."1</t>
    <t s="1">"This was the dedication of the altar..."2</t>
    <t s="2">Now, it is known that one of the reasons why on Chanukah we read the offerings of the princes3</t>
    <t s="3">is because on Chanukah they inaugurated4</t>
    <t s="4">the altar5,</t>
    <t s="5">similar to the dedication of the altar</t>
    <t s="6">(the first time)</t>
    <t s="7">through the offerings of the princes.</t>
    <t s="8">From this it is understood</t>
    <t s="9">that the eight days of Chanukah are parallel to the eight days of the inauguration.</t>
    <t s="10">And just as the eight days of the inauguration are divided into two,</t>
    <t s="11">the seven days of the inauguration and the eighth day,</t>
    <t s="12">so too is it regarding the eight days of Chanukah,</t>
    <t s="13">that the eighth day of Chanukah is called</t>
    <t s="14">(according to the custom of Israel)</t>
    <t s="15">also by a name of its own,</t>
    <t s="16">"Zos Chanukah."</t>
    <t s="17">[And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="18">that this is also why the Torah reading on the eighth day of Chanukah is much more than the seven days before it,</t>
    <t s="19">for on the first seven days they read only two princes each day6</t>
    <t s="20">and on the eighth day of Chanukah they read five princes, and also "This was the dedication of the altar" and the beginning of the portion of "Behaaloscha" regarding the lamps7,</t>
    <t s="21">for the addition in the Torah reading indicates the greatness of the day].</t>
    <t s="22">And it is explained in the discourse "Baruch She'asah Nissim" of the Alter Rebbe with glosses and notes etc. of the Tzemach Tzedek8,</t>
    <t s="23">that the eighth day</t>
    <t s="24">[of the inauguration, and likewise the eighth day]</t>
    <t s="25">of Chanukah is Malchus,</t>
    <t s="26">and therefore it is called "Zos Chanukah,"</t>
    <t s="27">for "Zos" is9</t>
    <t s="28">Malchus10.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the eighth has two aspects: being above the seven (Binah or Chochmah) and being below them (Malchus), with the connection between them enabling the flow into Malchus.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, it is known11</t>
    <t s="2">that regarding the eighth there are two matters.</t>
    <t s="3">That the eighth is above the seven that precede it</t>
    <t s="4">[similar to the explanation of the letters of the word "Az,"</t>
    <t s="5">the Aleph riding upon the Zayin12],</t>
    <t s="6">for the seven are the seven emotional attributes and the eighth is Binah.</t>
    <t s="7">And that the eighth is Malchus, which is below the seven emotional attributes.</t>
    <t s="8">And likewise regarding the eighth day of the inauguration,</t>
    <t s="9">it is stated in Likkutei Torah13</t>
    <t s="10">that there are two explanations of this.</t>
    <t s="11">That the eighth day of the inauguration is above the seven days of the inauguration,</t>
    <t s="12">for the seven days of the inauguration are in Binah and the eighth day of the inauguration is Chochmah14.</t>
    <t s="13">And that the eighth day of the inauguration is Malchus.</t>
    <t s="14">And the mediation between the two explanations is15,</t>
    <t s="15">that in order for there to be a flow into Malchus</t>
    <t s="16">(the eighth that is below the seven),</t>
    <t s="17">it is specifically through the flow being from a more elevated place</t>
    <t s="18">(that is above the seven).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
